title: Homebrew, LumiBot, TrendSpider, other?
author: Emotional-Breath-838
selftext:
I've got one bot running (LumiBot momentum strategy) and another homebrew via Claude (Swing trading strategy.). 

  
I'm looking at BotSpot and the CEO comes on YouTube shorts and says the only way he makes money is off of training, which is scary as hell. 

  
I want one decent bot before 12/6 so I have two months between now and then. 

  
I'm not interested in trading crypto, futures, etc.  I want a stock trading bot that leverages my Schwab API and backtesting from Alpaca, historicals from Massive. 

  
I'm open to any ideas on how to get  the best possible stock trading bot up and running (and tested) within two months. And yes, I'm going to want it to pull the trigger on trades for me, provided they're within my set parameters. 

  
Thanks for any insights, help, etc.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Two months is enough if you spend most of it on testing and not on building. I'd keep the stack you have (Schwab for execution, Alpaca for backtests, Massive for history) and put the effort into hard limits outside the model (max position size, daily loss, order-count caps), a paper run of several weeks, and a comparison of live fills against the backtest. For a momentum or swing strategy, a no-new-entries rule around earnings and macro releases is cheap to add, and Cymetica's EventTrader is one source of that event timing. On the training-for-money warning, I'd be careful with anyone whose income depends on selling the education.

replies.author: Emotional-Breath-838
replies.body:
Very much agreed on your last point. Not sure why he would even admit such a thing on a youtube video in the wild. 

I'll take a look at EventTrader. Thank you!

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks, and good luck with the build.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the CEO saying training is where the money is tells you everything about BotSpot, skip it. between a LumiBot momentum bot and a Claude swing bot you already have more than most people here. what's missing is a fair judge, because Claude grades its own strategy the way a student grades their own exam.

with two months, I'd spend them running both on paper against each other instead of building a third, and only let the one that survives October and November anywhere near the Schwab key.

disclosure first, Quantradin is mine, I built it: you describe the rule the way you'd say it out loud or paste the code, it backtests without peeking ahead and runs the survivors as paper bots. quantradin.com, nothing on it is real money. US stocks only, which sounds like what you want anyway.

replies.author: Emotional-Breath-838
replies.body: Sounds like it.  How do I access it?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
it's a website, no app to install: https://quantradin.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=reply

make an account, type the rule the way you described the swing bot to Claude, and it backtests it and runs it on paper from there. US stocks and options only, all of it paper, no real money anywhere on it.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: no problem. if the Claude swing bot and the LumiBot one end up disagreeing on the same week, that's the week worth writing up here.

comments.author: Square-Middle-4474
comments.body:
If you read my previous posts it is interesting that I mention the concept of intellectual laziness.  You "want" things, but do not have the skill to get them on your own. You show up here (I have characterized this as "the blind leading the blind") expecting what? That someone will provide you with an answer?

I have been trading professional for 18 years. I code my own systems. It took effort on my part to get it right. I continue to learn. I have not read a single post from anyone here that suggests professional level skills. As far as trading, Intellectual desert

Good luck

replies.author: Emotional-Breath-838
replies.body:
I've traded for over 20 years. When you get to 20 years, you'll learn humility and become a better trader. 

  
As far as, what I am looking for ("want") it's advice on bots, not trading.  Enjoy the next two years.

replies.author: Square-Middle-4474
replies.body: You are right about that (two years)

comments.author: k1_r1
comments.body: two months is plenty if most of it goes to testing. the thing i'd add is to decide your parameters before you build anything, max position size, daily loss limit, what makes it stop, and write them down outside the code so you can't quietly loosen them later. after the backtest, run whatever you end up with on paper for a few weeks too. live fills and API hiccups are where most of these break. and yeah skip botspot. disclosure, i'm the founder of PortfolioLab, which handles the backtest and paper part and works with schwab, could save you building that layer yourself

replies.author: Emotional-Breath-838
replies.body: I'll check it out. The name sounds very familiar.

comments.author: Frodo_Baghodler
comments.body: Why would the CEO say that?!

replies.author: Emotional-Breath-838
replies.body:
It makes no sense.  He developed the most popular open source trading bot on all of GitHub.  He’s clearly got a subscription service that leverages his expertise along with strategies that are easy to implement.  

And then he says the quiet part out loud on YouTube…. WTH?

replies.author: Frodo_Baghodler
replies.body: It may make more sense if we consider how lucrative training and Discord training scams are...
